subject: swell shark
title: This Shark Doubles Its Size in Seconds So Nothing Can Pull It Out

scenes.text: Grab this shark, and it swells to twice its size.
The swell shark hides in rocky crevices off California by day. Under a metre long, and harmless to people.
Threatened, it bends into a U, grabs its own tail in its mouth, and gulps water into its stomach.
Within seconds it's twice as big and wedged in the rock. A predator can't bite it or yank it free.
Later it releases the water and shrinks back. It can do the same with air, and letting it out makes a dog-like bark.
Under blue light, its skin even glows bright green. A shark that inflates, barks and glows, and nobody can pull it out.

description:
The swell shark can double its size in seconds by swallowing water, wedging itself into a rock crevice so predators cannot bite or dislodge it.
Cephaloscyllium ventriosum lives on rocky reefs and kelp beds in the eastern Pacific, mostly at 5 to 40 metres, and reaches about 110 cm. When threatened it curls into a U, grips its tail fin in its mouth and takes water, or air, into its stomach until it is roughly twice its normal size; when it releases air it makes a dog-like bark. Its skin is biofluorescent, first reported in 2014, and glows bright green under blue light thanks to pigments identified in 2019.
Which defence is better: this, or a pufferfish?
first_comment: A shark that inflates, barks and glows green. Which animal defence would you want for yourself?
